title: Matching Finance Term to Asset Life
context: Consider a manufacturer that already carries a high proportion of loan capital and must choose how to fund a multi-year production plant versus routine materials purchases. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditures on assets used over many years should normally be matched with long-term finance.
The only relevant criterion when choosing a source of finance is the absolute interest rate, so matching term to asset life and gearing risk can be ignored.
Interest is the sole cost element businesses must consider when comparing loans with share issues.
High gearing automatically disqualifies a firm from using any form of short-term trade credit for materials.
Capital expenditure on a warehouse extension should be funded from weekly supplier credit without regard to asset life.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Long-lived asset spending calls for long-term finance so repayment timing aligns with the period of use.
FALSE — Cost matters, but intended use and current gearing also shape the appropriate choice.
FALSE — Share and bond issues carry administration costs that must be weighed against borrowing.
FALSE — High gearing complicates further borrowing but does not ban routine short-term credit for revenue spending.
FALSE — Long-lived assets require long-term finance; short-term supplier credit mismatches repayment to asset life.

title: Administration Costs in Finance Comparison
context: Analyze the role of costs—including interest and issuance expenses—in selecting an appropriate source of finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Revenue expenditures on production inputs should always be matched with a twenty-year mortgage loan.
Administration costs of issuing bonds are irrelevant when comparing finance sources for any project.
Revenue expenditures such as buying materials for current production can safely be financed by short-term sources.
A business never needs to consider its current gearing when choosing how to pay for weekly raw materials.
Revenue expenditure on materials consumed in current production must be financed exclusively through share issues.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Long-term debt would mismatch repayment to the brief consumption period of materials.
FALSE — Bond issuance costs are part of the cost criterion in finance selection.
TRUE — Short-cycle materials need short-term credit such as overdrafts or trade credit.
FALSE — Gearing affects overall finance strategy even when short-term credit suits revenue spending.
FALSE — Materials for current production suit short-term sources, not equity issues for long-lived capital.

title: Revenue Spending and Short-Term Credit
context: Review how capital expenditures on long-lived assets should be matched with the term of finance chosen. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A highly geared business will always obtain new loans at the same interest rate as a low-debt rival.
Intended use of funds is unrelated to whether finance should be short-term or long-term.
The absolute interest rate is the only criterion when choosing finance, so matching term to asset life is unnecessary.
A highly geared business may struggle to raise further credit except at higher interest rates and/or against additional collateral.
High gearing means a firm should ignore issuance administration costs when comparing share finance with bonds.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Lenders often charge higher interest or demand collateral when loan capital is already high.
FALSE — Intended use is a core criterion linking expenditure type to finance maturity.
FALSE — Intended use and gearing also matter; interest alone does not govern finance choice.
TRUE — High gearing makes lenders cautious and often raises the price or collateral demand of new debt.
FALSE — Administration costs for shares and bonds remain part of the cost criterion regardless of gearing.

title: Capital Expenditure and Long-Term Funding
context: Analyze how revenue expenditures on materials and other short-cycle inputs relate to short-term finance sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When loan capital is already high, internal funds or new equity investors can reduce insolvency risk relative to taking another large loan.
Only the intended use of funds counts as a cost when choosing between overdraft and trade credit.
A highly geared business can ignore its financial situation if the interest rate on a new loan appears low.
Administration costs incurred when issuing shares or bonds form part of the cost comparison among finance sources.
Capital expenditure on a ten-year production line should be funded from a thirty-day trade credit facility alone.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Retained earnings or investors avoid adding further mandatory repayment obligations.
FALSE — Intended use is a separate criterion from cost; both matter alongside financial position.
FALSE — Low quoted interest does not override high gearing and repayment risk in finance choice.
TRUE — Issuance expenses belong to the cost criterion alongside interest on loans and credit.
FALSE — Long-lived capital projects need long-term finance, not brief supplier credit.

title: Three Criteria for Finance Choice
context: Consider a neighbourhood bakery that needs new ovens lasting many years while also buying flour and sugar for weekly production cycles. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When several sources of finance are available, a business will most probably weigh costs, intended use, and current financial situation.
Equity finance carries no cost element because issuing shares never involves administration expenses.
Capital expenditure on equipment with a long useful life should be matched with long-term finance.
A business already carrying a high proportion of loan capital may have difficulties obtaining more credit from lenders.
Lenders may offer further funds to a highly geared business only at a higher interest rate and/or if collateral can be provided.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Cost, use, and financial position are the main decision criteria in the chapter framework.
FALSE — Share issuance incurs administration costs that must be weighed against loans.
TRUE — Multi-year assets call for finance whose maturity aligns with years of service.
TRUE — Heavy existing debt makes lenders cautious about extending additional credit.
TRUE — Stricter pricing or collateral often accompanies new loans to highly geared borrowers.

title: High Gearing and Credit Access
context: Analyze why a business with a high proportion of loan capital may prefer internal funds or investors over additional debt. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditure and revenue expenditure both require identical long-term mortgage funding regardless of use.
Such a business should rather try to use internal sources of finance and/or find investors willing to provide funds.
Because loans must be repaid, a high proportion of loan capital can increase the risk of insolvency.
Costs of finance include interest payments on loans and credit as well as administration costs for issuing shares or bonds.
Financial funds used for capital expenditures on long-lived assets require long-term sources of finance.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Expenditure type determines appropriate finance maturity; they are not interchangeable.
TRUE — Retained earnings or investor funds avoid adding further mandatory repayment obligations.
TRUE — Repayment pressure on existing and new loans raises insolvency risk when debt is already high.
TRUE — The cost criterion covers both interest and issuance-related administration expenses.
TRUE — Asset purchases with extended useful lives call for comparably long finance.

title: Cost Criterion in Finance Selection
context: Review how administration costs of issuing shares or bonds enter the cost comparison among finance sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Matching long-term finance to capital expenditure spreads repayment over the years the asset generates benefits.
A high geared business may obtain further credit only if it can offer collateral acceptable to lenders.
Investors or business partners may supply funds when additional loans would worsen insolvency risk.
Interest on loans and credit is excluded from the cost criterion when comparing finance sources.
Funding a new factory building exclusively through supplier credit for raw materials matches finance maturity correctly.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Aligning maturity to asset life reduces cash-flow strain from premature principal repayment.
TRUE — Collateral often becomes a condition for new credit when existing loan capital is substantial.
TRUE — Equity-type injections reduce reliance on repayable debt when gearing is already elevated.
FALSE — Interest on loans and credit is explicitly part of the cost criterion.
FALSE — Factory construction is capital expenditure needing long-term finance, not material trade credit.

title: Intended Use and Finance Maturity
context: Analyze the insolvency risk that arises when loan capital must be repaid while the business already carries heavy debt. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Interest is one cost element, but intended use and gearing also guide finance selection.
Businesses with several finance options most probably decide using costs, intended use, and current financial situation.
Purchasing assets that will be used over some or even many years counts as capital expenditure requiring long-term finance.
Interest payments on loans and credit are part of the cost criterion when choosing among finance sources.
Administration costs of share issues are counted as intended use rather than as finance costs.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Cost, use, and financial situation are joint criteria, not interest alone.
TRUE — All three criteria—cost, use, and position—frame realistic finance choice.
TRUE — Asset spending with multi-year benefits should be funded over a comparable long horizon.
TRUE — Borrowing costs include interest, which businesses weigh when selecting finance.
FALSE — Issuance costs are part of the cost criterion, not a description of fund use.

title: Gearing Collateral and Insolvency Risk
context: Consider a regional retailer financing seasonal stock with supplier credit while planning a long-term store refurbishment from retained earnings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Buying material that is used for production within the operating cycle is revenue expenditure that can safely be financed by short-term sources.
Bond issues carry both coupon interest and upfront flotation expenses that enter the finance comparison.
Purchasing components for assembly within the month is revenue expenditure that can safely be financed by short-term sources.
Lenders may be reluctant to offer more funds to a business that already has a high proportion of loan capital.
Further credit to a highly geared business may be available only at a higher interest rate.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Short-cycle inputs align with short-term finance such as trade credit or overdrafts.
TRUE — Bond finance price reflects interest plus related administration costs.
TRUE — Short-cycle production inputs align with brief credit facilities.
TRUE — Heavy debt loads make creditors cautious about increasing exposure.
TRUE — Risk pricing often raises interest when gearing is already elevated.

title: Integrated Finance Decision Criteria
context: Analyze why lenders may demand collateral or charge higher interest when extending credit to a highly geared firm. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Internal finance or investor funds avoid creating new mandatory debt repayment schedules.
Interest on loans and credit is a cost element businesses compare when choosing finance sources.
Intended use of funds still matters even when one source appears cheaper on interest alone.
When loan capital is already high, a business must reject internal funds and investors because only debt can fund expansion.
Capital expenditure on machinery, plant, or vehicles used over many years requires long-term finance.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Equity and retained earnings do not carry the same contractual repayment burden as loans.
TRUE — Borrowing carries explicit interest that forms part of the cost criterion.
TRUE — Matching finance term to expenditure type remains necessary regardless of nominal interest.
FALSE — Internal funds and investors are recommended when further loans would worsen repayment pressure.
TRUE — Long-lived assets should be funded over a horizon comparable to their useful life.

title: Issuance Costs Versus Loan Interest
context: Review the three main decision criteria when several sources of finance are available to a business. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Financial funds for capital expenditures require long-term finance because assets will be used over years.
Costs comprise interest on loans and administration costs of issuing shares or bonds.
Choosing finance based only on the headline interest rate ignores intended use and current gearing.
Issuing bonds instead of bank loans eliminates repayment risk for a highly geared business.
Revenue expenditure on production inputs should always be matched with bond finance maturing in twenty years.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Multi-year asset spending calls for long-term funding to match benefit periods.
TRUE — Both interest and issuance costs belong in the cost comparison.
FALSE — Cost is one of three criteria; use and financial situation also govern choice.
FALSE — Bonds are still loan capital that must be repaid with interest; gearing risk remains.
FALSE — Short-cycle materials suit short-term finance, not long-term bond funding.

title: Capital and Revenue Finance Matching
context: Analyze how matching finance maturity to expenditure type reduces repayment pressure on routine operations. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Such a firm should rather try internal sources of finance and/or investors willing to provide funds.
A business with a high proportion of loan capital may have difficulties obtaining more credit.
Administration costs incurred when issuing shares or bonds should be weighed alongside interest on loans.
Revenue expenditure such as buying materials for production can safely be financed by short-term sources.
High gearing removes any need to compare administration costs when issuing shares to raise funds.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Retained earnings and investor funds reduce reliance on new repayable debt when gearing is high.
TRUE — Heavy loan capital makes additional borrowing harder to secure.
TRUE — Issuance fees belong in the cost criterion next to loan interest.
TRUE — Short-cycle spending fits short-term credit without lengthy principal schedules.
FALSE — Share issuance costs remain part of the cost criterion even when gearing motivates equity.

title: Working Capital and Short-Term Credit
context: Consider a construction firm covering payroll gaps with short-term bank loans while shareholders debate whether to inject equity instead of adding more debt. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A business with a high proportion of loan capital might have difficulties obtaining more credit.
High gearing means capital expenditure should be funded only through additional bank loans at any interest rate offered.
Lenders may extend credit to a highly geared business only if acceptable collateral can be offered.
Revenue expenditure must never use short-term trade credit when the balance sheet already lists any loan capital.
Administration costs of bond issues are ignored because only equity carries issuance expenses.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Existing heavy debt makes creditors wary of increasing exposure.
FALSE — The chapter advises against piling on debt when gearing is high; internal or investor funds are preferred.
TRUE — Security requirements often accompany new loans when loan capital is already substantial.
FALSE — Short-term finance for revenue spending remains appropriate even when long-term debt is already high.
FALSE — Both shares and bonds carry administration costs in the cost criterion.

title: Lender Reluctance Under High Gearing
context: Analyze how buying assets used over many years differs from buying production materials in finance-matching logic. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditure on a multi-year production plant should be funded from weekly overdraft drawings alone.
Capital expenditure on assets that will be used over some or even many years requires long-term finance.
Costs, intended use, and current financial situation are the main criteria when choosing among finance sources.
Funding a multi-year production plant solely through repeated overdraft drawings mismatches short-term finance to capital expenditure.
Treating the absolute interest rate as the only selection criterion ignores intended use and current gearing.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Long-lived plant assets need long-term finance, not reliance on short overdraft facilities.
TRUE — Asset life governs the appropriate maturity of finance.
TRUE — The chapter presents this trio as the decision framework.
TRUE — Long-lived assets require long-term finance, not rolling short-term overdraft reliance.
TRUE — The chapter requires weighing cost together with use and financial situation.

title: Insolvency Risk from Heavy Loan Capital
context: Review how internal sources of finance can reduce insolvency risk for a business already reliant on loan capital. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit from suppliers postpones payment for inputs consumed within the operating cycle.
Revenue expenditure on raw materials requires a bond issue with a fifteen-year maturity.
High gearing guarantees unlimited access to cheap long-term loans for any capital project.
Matching finance maturity to expenditure type is still required when comparing loan interest with bond coupons.
When loan capital is already high, internal sources of finance and investors can be preferable to another large loan.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Supplier credit is a standard short-term source for routine purchases.
FALSE — Long-term bond finance mismatches the brief consumption period of materials.
FALSE — Heavy debt typically restricts rather than expands cheap credit availability.
TRUE — Asset life and gearing shape finance choice beyond nominal interest rates.
TRUE — Retained earnings and investor funds avoid new fixed repayment obligations.

title: Interest Issuance Costs and Intended Use
context: Consider a hotel operator with heavy existing borrowings that must fund a new wing through bonds, an overdraft, or reinvested profit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Revenue expenditure on production materials can safely be financed by short-term sources even when loan capital is already high.
High gearing complicates obtaining further long-term loans but does not ban appropriate short-term finance for revenue spending.
Because loans must be repaid, a high proportion of loan capital can be a burden that increases insolvency risk.
Costs, intended use, and current financial situation together guide finance choice when several sources exist.
Financing a multi-year production facility exclusively through short-term overdraft drawings mismatches revenue-type credit to capital expenditure.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Short-cycle materials still suit trade credit or overdrafts regardless of balance-sheet debt.
TRUE — Gearing mainly affects appetite for additional long-term debt, not all short-term working-capital credit.
TRUE — Fixed repayment schedules on heavy debt threaten solvency if income weakens.
TRUE — No single criterion overrides the other two in the chapter framework.
TRUE — Long-lived plant assets require long-term finance, not rolling short-term overdraft reliance.

title: Long-Term Assets and Finance Horizon
context: Review how a business with several finance options will most probably weigh cost, use, and financial situation together. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A highly geared business may obtain further credit only at higher interest and/or if collateral is provided.
Capital expenditure on machinery used over many years should be matched with long-term finance.
When several funding routes exist, selection usually weighs costs, the purpose of the funds, and the firm's gearing.
Ignoring administration costs when issuing shares or bonds understates the true cost of those finance sources.
A high proportion of loan capital can be a burden because loans must be repaid, raising insolvency risk.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Lenders tighten pricing and security when loan capital is already substantial.
TRUE — Multi-year machinery calls for finance spanning comparable years.
TRUE — Costs, intended use, and financial situation jointly shape the choice.
TRUE — Issuance expenses belong in the cost criterion alongside loan interest.
TRUE — Mandatory debt service on heavy loans threatens solvency when cash flow is insufficient.

title: Core Finance Matching Principles
context: Analyze the trade-off between debt interest and the administration costs of raising equity or bond finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Revenue expenditure on weekly supplies must be financed through a twenty-year mortgage.
Share issues carry no administration costs, so only loan interest needs comparison.
All production materials must be financed through long-term bond issues regardless of consumption speed.
Costs, intended use, and financial situation jointly determine finance choice among available sources for expansion projects.
Administration costs of bond issues belong in the cost comparison with loan interest.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Short-cycle revenue spending suits short-term sources, not long-term mortgages.
FALSE — Equity and bond issues both involve administration costs in the chapter framework.
FALSE — Long-term bonds mismatch the brief use period of routine materials.
TRUE — All three chapter criteria apply together.
TRUE — Issuance costs are part of the cost criterion alongside borrowing interest.

title: Gearing Traps in Finance Choice
context: Review why additional loan capital can become a burden when repayment obligations already strain cash flow. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditure on assets used over many years still requires long-term finance despite high gearing.
Capital expenditure on vehicles used for ten years should be funded from thirty-day supplier credit.
High gearing removes interest from the list of costs businesses must compare.
High gearing means revenue expenditure must be reclassified as capital expenditure before any finance is chosen.
Collateral requirements prove that interest is the only cost businesses need to compare among finance sources.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Asset life dictates long-term funding needs even when additional debt is costly.
FALSE — Long-lived vehicles are capital expenditure requiring long-term finance.
FALSE — Interest on loans remains part of the cost criterion at any gearing level.
FALSE — Expenditure type is determined by use and asset life, not by renaming it when debt is high.
FALSE — Collateral relates to lender risk from gearing; interest and issuance costs remain separate cost elements.

title: Single Criterion Misconceptions
context: Consider a freight carrier renewing its vehicle fleet with a long-term bank loan while purchasing fuel and tyres on trade credit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Revenue expenditure on materials for current production can safely be financed by short-term sources.
High gearing automatically makes share issuance free of administration costs.
Costs comprise interest on loans and credit plus administration costs for issuing shares or bonds.
High gearing may leave lenders reluctant except at higher interest or with collateral, favouring internal funds or investors.
Revenue expenditure on flour and sugar for weekly baking must be funded through a twenty-year bond.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Short-cycle inputs align with trade credit or overdrafts.
FALSE — Share and bond administration costs still enter the cost criterion regardless of gearing.
TRUE — The cost criterion covers interest and issuance expenses.
TRUE — Elevated debt tightens credit terms and makes non-debt finance attractive.
FALSE — Short-cycle ingredients suit short-term finance, not multi-year bond funding.

title: Revenue Inputs and Trade Credit
context: Review why revenue expenditure on inputs used for current production aligns with short-term finance sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditure on a ten-year asset should be funded from trade credit for raw materials.
Using short-term credit for revenue expenditure avoids tying multi-year repayment schedules to inputs quickly consumed.
Comparing a bank loan with a bond issue requires weighing interest against bond issuance expenses.
Share issues involve administration costs that should enter the cost side of the finance decision.
Only intended use matters, so a highly geared firm may ignore repayment risk when taking new loans.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Long-lived assets need long-term finance, not supplier credit for materials.
TRUE — Short-term finance suits spending that rolls over each operating period.
TRUE — Bond interest and flotation costs together shape the price of that debt source.
TRUE — Equity raising is not cost-free; administration costs form part of the comparison.
FALSE — Financial situation and gearing affect whether further debt is prudent even when use is matched.

title: Capital Projects and Debt Capacity
context: Analyze how high gearing may leave lenders reluctant to offer more funds except on stricter terms. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Internal funds are never preferable to loans regardless of how high loan capital already is.
Administration costs of share issues are excluded from cost comparisons because shares carry no fees.
Revenue expenditures on weekly ingredients can safely be financed through trade credit or overdraft facilities.
Revenue expenditure on materials for production must be financed exclusively through twenty-year mortgage loans.
When gearing is elevated, adding another large loan can worsen repayment pressure on cash flow.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — The chapter explicitly favours internal funds or investors when gearing is high.
FALSE — Share issuance involves administration costs that must be weighed against loan interest.
TRUE — Working-capital spending suits short-term credit without multi-year repayment tails.
FALSE — Short-cycle materials suit short-term finance, not long-term mortgage loans.
TRUE — Additional loans compound fixed repayment obligations when debt is already substantial.

title: Issuance Costs Versus Borrowing
context: Review how retained earnings and new investors can strengthen finance choice when external credit is costly. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Administration costs of share or bond issues are excluded from the cost comparison when choosing finance.
A low headline interest rate does not by itself prove a loan is cheaper than equity once issuance fees are included.
Buying material used for production within the current cycle is revenue expenditure suited to short-term finance.
Buying assets that will be used over some or even many years is capital expenditure requiring long-term finance.
Internal sources of finance can be preferable when loan capital is already high because they avoid new repayment obligations.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Issuance costs belong in the cost criterion alongside loan interest.
TRUE — Total cost includes both ongoing charges and upfront issuance expenses.
TRUE — Inputs consumed quickly fit short-term credit without lengthy repayment schedules.
TRUE — Multi-year assets should be funded over a horizon matching useful life.
TRUE — Retained earnings do not create new mandatory debt service like another loan would.

title: Short-Term Sources for Materials
context: Consider an agricultural cooperative retaining member profits internally while lenders demand higher interest on any further long-term credit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A highly geared business should always add another large loan rather than use internal funds or investors.
Capital expenditure on assets used over many years can safely rely on thirty-day trade credit alone.
Because loans must be repaid, a high proportion of loan capital can burden the business with insolvency risk.
Interest on loans is the only cost element, so administration costs of share or bond issues need not be compared.
High gearing means a firm should ignore its financial situation and select finance solely by the lowest advertised interest rate.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — The chapter favours internal funds or investors when gearing is already high.
FALSE — Multi-year assets require long-term finance, not brief supplier credit.
TRUE — Debt service on heavy loans threatens solvency if revenues fall short.
FALSE — Administration costs for shares and bonds are part of the cost criterion alongside loan interest.
FALSE — Financial situation and gearing still matter even when one source quotes a low interest rate.

title: Highly Geared Firm Strategy
context: Review how collateral requirements may accompany new credit offers to highly geared borrowers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditure on expansion assets used over many years requires long-term finance.
Revenue expenditure on routine inputs can safely use short-term finance.
High gearing guarantees that every lender will extend further credit at the same rate as before the debt build-up.
High gearing may make lenders offer credit only at higher interest or with collateral.
Bond flotation costs should be ignored when comparing debt sources because only coupon interest represents the price of bond finance.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Long-lived expansion assets need long-term funding.
TRUE — Short-cycle spending fits brief credit facilities.
FALSE — Lenders typically tighten terms when loan capital is already substantial, not maintain identical pricing.
TRUE — Stricter terms often accompany new loans to highly geared firms.
FALSE — Flotation costs belong in the total cost of bond finance alongside coupon interest.

title: Collateral and Credit Pricing
context: Analyze how administration costs affect the comparison between issuing shares and taking a bank loan. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Internal funds or investors can reduce insolvency risk when loan capital is already high.
Elevated gearing points the firm toward retained funds or new investors rather than stacking another major loan.
Administration costs of issuing shares or bonds belong to the cost criterion alongside loan interest.
A finance decision based only on loan interest ignores flotation and related costs of market issues.
Revenue expenditure on weekly ingredients requires bond finance maturing after fifteen years.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Non-debt finance avoids adding repayable obligations when debt is heavy.
TRUE — High loan capital makes internal equity or outside investors preferable.
TRUE — Issuance fees are part of the cost criterion next to borrowing interest.
TRUE — Total cost of bond or share finance includes non-interest fees.
FALSE — Long-term bonds mismatch the quick consumption of production materials.

title: Balancing Cost Use and Position
context: Review the link between loan repayment obligations and the risk of insolvency in highly geared businesses. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Intended use still requires matching long-term finance to capital expenditure on multi-year assets.
When several sources of finance are available, decision-making most probably weighs costs, intended use, and financial situation.
Financial funds for capital expenditures require long-term finance because benefits extend over years.
Revenue expenditures on production inputs can safely use short-term sources.
High gearing may mean credit is offered only at higher interest and/or with collateral.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Asset life determines finance maturity regardless of nominal coupon or dividend.
TRUE — All three criteria jointly determine appropriate finance.
TRUE — Asset spending with extended life needs long-term funding.
TRUE — Materials consumed in the cycle fit short-term finance.
TRUE — Lenders price and secure new loans more strictly when debt is heavy.

title: Long-Term Finance for Plant Assets
context: Consider a dental practice choosing between a multi-year premises loan, supplier credit for consumables, and funds from new investor-partners. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Capital expenditure on machinery, plant, or vehicles used over many years should be matched with long-term finance.
Capital expenditure on a warehouse used for decades should be funded exclusively through thirty-day trade credit.
High gearing means intended use no longer influences whether finance should be short or long term.
Matching finance maturity to expenditure type is optional when the quoted loan interest rate is low.
A business should finance ten-year equipment and weekly materials from the same thirty-day overdraft without distinction.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Long-lived assets require finance whose term spans years of service.
FALSE — Long-lived buildings are capital expenditure needing long-term finance.
FALSE — Intended use remains a core criterion regardless of gearing level.
FALSE — Intended use and gearing still matter even when nominal interest appears attractive.
FALSE — Different expenditure types require different finance maturities.

title: Overdraft Misuse for Capital Spending
context: Review why trade credit and overdrafts suit revenue-type spending better than multi-year asset projects. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: High gearing means lenders will always match the lowest market interest rate on new loans.
Costs include interest on loans and administration costs when issuing shares or bonds.
Costs of finance exclude interest because lenders provide credit without charge.
Collateral requirements prove that revenue expenditure must always be financed through long-term bonds.
Insolvency risk arises only from equity finance because shareholders can withdraw capital overnight without notice.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Heavy debt often leads to higher pricing or refusal, not automatic low rates.
TRUE — Both interest and issuance fees enter cost comparisons.
FALSE — Interest on loans and credit is explicitly part of the cost criterion.
FALSE — Revenue spending still suits short-term finance; collateral relates to lender risk on new debt.
FALSE — Share capital is not repayable like loans; insolvency risk is tied to debt service.

title: Interest Alone Fallacy
context: Analyze how a firm's current financial situation shapes whether further loan capital is prudent. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Interest is irrelevant to finance choice because lenders never charge for credit.
A business with high gearing may prefer internal funds or investors over additional large loans.
Revenue expenditure on materials must be financed through share issues because equity has no administration costs.
Because loans must be repaid, heavy loan capital raises insolvency risk.
High gearing automatically makes bond interest zero for any new borrowing.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Interest on loans is explicitly part of the cost criterion.
TRUE — Further debt is often unwise when repayment obligations are already substantial.
FALSE — Share issues carry administration costs and materials suit short-term finance, not equity raises.
TRUE — Debt service burden threatens solvency when loan capital is high.
FALSE — Bond and loan interest remain part of the cost criterion at any gearing level.

title: Trade Credit for Revenue Spending
context: Consider a software startup weighing share issuance costs against a short-term credit line for routine operating expenses. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: When gearing is elevated, internal finance or investors may be preferable to stacking on more repayable debt.
Share issuance is costless, so only bond coupons need comparison with bank interest.
Capital expenditure on long-lived assets requires long-term finance.
Businesses choose finance using costs, intended use, and current financial situation when several sources are available.
Interest on loans and administration costs of share or bond issues belong to the cost criterion.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Equity and retained funds avoid new mandatory debt service when loan capital is already high.
FALSE — Share issues involve administration costs that enter finance comparisons.
TRUE — Multi-year assets call for long-term funding.
TRUE — The chapter's trio of criteria frames finance decisions.
TRUE — Cost includes both interest and issuance administration expenses.

title: Asset Life and Repayment Schedules
context: Analyze why issuance costs for bonds must be weighed alongside interest when comparing debt sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: High gearing may push a firm toward internal funds or investors and raises insolvency risk from loan repayment.
Revenue expenditure on weekly supplies should be funded through twenty-year loans.
Lenders may require collateral before extending further credit to a business with a high proportion of loan capital.
Capital expenditure on assets used over years requires long-term finance.
Internal funds or investors can be preferable when loan capital is already high because loans must be repaid.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Heavy debt limits further borrowing and repayment risk favours non-debt finance.
FALSE — Short-cycle revenue spending suits short-term sources, not long-term loans.
TRUE — Security is commonly demanded when existing loan capital is already substantial.
TRUE — Multi-year assets call for long-term funding.
TRUE — Avoiding new debt reduces repayment burden and insolvency risk when gearing is high.

title: Gearing and Investor Alternatives
context: Review how intended use and gearing interact when a business selects among internal and external finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Interest on loans is the only cost element in finance selection.
A business with several finance sources will most probably decide using costs, intended use, and current financial situation.
Capital expenditure requires long-term finance; revenue expenditure can safely use short-term sources.
Matching long-term funding to multi-year assets spreads repayment over the period benefits are earned.
